anti_patterns: Deploy-and-forget immutable logic holding real value without audit, formal verification, or bug-bounty review: the DAO-style bug cannot be patched in place
Letting contracts pull real-world facts directly instead of via an oracle feed: nondeterministic I/O breaks validator consensus
Reentrant external calls before state effects (checks-effects-interactions violation): the classic draining attack surface
Storing personal data or large blobs onchain: immutable PII conflicts with erasure duties and state bloat raises costs for every node
Upgradeable-proxy-everywhere by default: admin-key upgradability reintroduces the trusted intermediary the pattern exists to remove
Unbounded loops and dynamic arrays iterated onchain: gas metering turns them into denial-of-service vectors or stuck funds
avoid_when: Business rules change frequently or need human discretion, renegotiation, or legal interpretation
Sub-second latency or high sustained throughput (>thousands of TPS) is required
Data must be correctable or deletable (PII, mutable records) without offset-transaction ceremony
A single trusted organization controls all parties and a signed database workflow would suffice
Computation is heavy, nondeterministic, or depends on off-chain APIs at execution time
Team lacks smart-contract security expertise and no audit budget exists
best_practices: Follow checks-effects-interactions and use audited guard libraries (e.g. OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard, SafeMath-equivalents) rather than hand-rolled controls
Keep contracts minimal and modular; isolate token, governance, and business logic so each surface stays auditable
Add emergency controls deliberately (pause, timelocked upgrade) and disclose the trust they reintroduce
Emit events for every material state transition so off-chain indexers and auditors can reconstruct history
Test against mainnet forks with fuzzing and invariant tests; run at least one independent audit before value-bearing deployment
Estimate and cap gas per function; prefer pull-over-push payments so one recipient cannot block disbursement
Pin a fixed compiler version, enable optimizer deliberately, and verify source on a block explorer at deployment
benefits: Automatic enforcement: predefined conditions execute without banks, brokers, or manual reconciliation
Trust minimization: counterparties verify code and execution history instead of trusting each other
Tamper-resistant settlement: replicated execution plus consensus makes unilateral alteration of outcomes infeasible
Composability: public contracts expose callable interfaces so new agreements build on deployed ones like open APIs
Deterministic auditability: every trigger, input, and state change is permanently recorded onchain
Disintermediated lifecycle: escrow, release, liquidation, and vesting run as code paths rather than institutional processes
component_types: Smart Contract: versioned code-plus-storage unit resident at an on-chain address with constructor, functions, and access guards
Virtual Machine Runtime: deterministic execution engine (EVM, WASM, chaincode container) replayed identically by every validator
Ledger State: replicated world state the contract reads and writes; changes commit only via consensus on the resulting state
Transaction and Event Interface: signed invocations in, emitted logs out; the only bridge between off-chain clients and on-chain logic
Metering and Endorsement Policy: gas schedule (public chains) or endorser-signature rules (Fabric) bounding and authorizing execution
Oracle Boundary: feed or request-response adapter supplying external facts deterministically since contracts cannot fetch the web themselves
Upgrade and Ownership Controls: proxy/delegation scaffolding or immutable deployment policy governing who can fix or retire the code
context: Multiple parties need a shared agreement executed exactly as written without relying on a trusted intermediary. Business rules (escrow release, collateral liquidation, royalty splits, access grants) are encoded as deterministic programs deployed to a blockchain address; participants trigger them with signed transactions and every validator re-executes the same logic to reach consensus on the outcome.
design_principles: Code Is the Agreement: terms must be fully specified in executable logic; ambiguity that needs a judge belongs offchain
Determinism by Construction: no randomness, wall-clock reads, or network calls inside execution; all validators must converge
Immutability by Default: assume deployed bytecode cannot be changed; design for correctness on first deployment
Minimal Onchain Footprint: store proofs, balances, and state roots onchain; keep documents, media, and PII offchain
Explicit Trust Boundaries: every external input arrives via transactions or oracles and must be validated at the boundary
Fail Closed: failed preconditions revert state rather than partially applying effects
name: smart-contract-pattern
references: Ethereum Community, Introduction to smart contracts — https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/smart-contracts/
Ethereum Community, Anatomy of smart contracts — https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/smart-contracts/anatomy/
Hyperledger Fabric Maintainers, Smart Contracts and Chaincode — https://hlf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/smartcontract/smartcontract.html
Chainalysis, What Is a Smart Contract? Definition, How It Works & Security Risks — https://www.chainalysis.com/glossary/smart-contracts/
tradeoffs: Immutability cuts both ways: deployed bugs are irreversible without pre-planned proxy or migration paths
Replicated execution is expensive: every validator runs every computation, so throughput is low and fees scale with complexity
Closed-world execution: contracts cannot observe off-chain events without an oracle, reintroducing a trust dependency
Determinism restricts expressiveness: no randomness, floating point freedom, or direct API calls inside contract logic
Key-based identity is unforgiving: lost or stolen keys mean lost control with no password-reset path
Composability couples risk: a vulnerability in a called contract propagates to every dependent within the same transaction
use_cases: DeFi lending pools that collateralize, accrue interest, and liquidate entirely in contract logic
Token issuance and transfer (ERC-20 fungible, ERC-721/1155 non-fungible) with programmatic mint and royalty rules
Escrow and conditional release: funds move only when delivery, milestone, or multisig conditions verify onchain
Supply-chain milestones releasing payment or custody transfer when sensor/oracle attestations arrive
On-chain governance and treasuries executing votes, vesting schedules, and disbursements without administrators
Parametric insurance paying out automatically when an oracle reports a qualifying event
